newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up as institutional buyers emerge.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up as institutional buyers emerge.

text.p: Stronger institutional demand from the U.S. pushed prices of Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) higher in London.
"It is not massive, but it is institutional business, which has been hard to come by in recent months," said one trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI gained 2.57 points or 3.75 percent, to 71.14 points, with the premium over the local market at 24.46 percent compared with yesterday's 20.39 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 24.76 points to 3,288.88.

"The locals are long at the moment and tending to follow the GDRs, but with the government desperately wanting to raise money for VSNL, the local market is not going to be allowed to fall," said the trader.
Indian overseas telephone monopoly VSNL aims to raise about $800 million from foreign investors in the first quarter.
GDR premiums have stretched out in the past month and hotels group EIH, a $40 million issue, is now on a 49 percent premium to the local stock.
The stock put on $1.20 to $27.00/$28.00 today.
Reliance, India's largest quoted company, added 94 cents to $13.25/$14.25.
"It still looks good value on a premium of eleven percent compared with 30-35 percent for most other blue chips," said the India trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index rose 3.73 points or 6.16 percent, to 64.37, a premium of 63.37 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 10.36 points to 621.41.
"There is not much stock out there and in pure dollar terms the market does look cheap," said a trader, who warned however that the country's acrimonious labour dispute may have some way to run.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 1.28 points or 1.33 percent, to 97.43, a premium of 7.48 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 144.41 points, or 2.10 percent, to 7,019.43 points.

The Chicago Mercantile Exchange and SIMEX are to launch stock index futures on Taiwan on Thursday, which traders said had improved sentiment and there are also rumours of a merger between three of the country's banks.
"The merger talk is probably rubbish but it has added fuel to the fire. Whatever the truth on that, people are loath to be caught short of stock in January," said one trader.
